arxiv.title: Order-Only On-Policy Distillation
arxiv.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own generations by matching the teacher's token probabilities. These probabilities entangle two kinds of information: which tokens the teacher prefers, and how confident it is. The latter reflects the teacher's own capacity and calibration, which a smaller student may be unable to reproduce. Because the teacher temperature changes these values without changing the ordering, OPD is also sensitive to the temperature choice. We ask whether the teacher's ordering of candidate tokens is enough, and propose Order-Only On-Policy Distillation (O$^{3}$PD). At each student-generated prefix, O$^{3}$PD trains the student to reproduce the order of the teacher's top-$K$ tokens, without fitting their probability values. The objective is therefore invariant to the teacher temperature and needs no temperature tuning. Across six teacher--student pairs, O$^{3}$PD outperforms OPD on the average over HMMT25, AIME24, and AIME25 in every pair, by up to 2.9 points, with gains of up to 5.6 points on AIME25. Other ranking losses yield similar gains, so the benefit comes from ordinal supervision itself. Analysis shows that O$^{3}$PD departs further from the teacher's probabilities than OPD, yet reproduces its ranking more faithfully and yields a stronger student. The ranking, not the probability values, thus carries the knowledge that on-policy distillation needs to transfer.
arxiv.titleZh: 仅序在线策略蒸馏（Order-Only On-Policy Distillation）
arxiv.summaryZh: 在线策略蒸馏（OPD）在学生自生成前缀上对齐教师的 token 概率，但概率值同时编码了教师的偏好排序与置信度校准，后者小模型难以复现，且对教师温度敏感。O³PD 改为只要求学生复现教师 top-K 候选 token 的排序、不拟合概率数值，目标对教师温度不变，无需调温。在六组师生模型对上，O³PD 在 HMMT25、AIME24、AIME25 上的平均分全部超过 OPD，最高提升 2.9 分，AIME25 上最高提升 5.6 分。分析显示它偏离教师概率更远，却更忠实地还原排序并得到更强的学生，提示蒸馏需迁移的是排序而非概率值。

arxiv.title: Consolidating Reasoning with Test-Time Training
arxiv.abstract: Effective multi-agent collaboration requires finalizing solutions from reasoning that is distributed across the individual attempts of many agents. However, useful intermediate reasoning can remain unexploited when collaboration is limited to voting on conclusions reached among individual agents, or aggregating long, noisy collections of reasoning trajectories in context. In this work, we propose TTT-Consolidate, a framework that uses multi-agent reasoning trajectories as adaptation data to improve a model's subsequent reasoning. TTT-Consolidate jointly consolidates trajectories into parametric representations through test-time training, then generates a new solution by conditioning on the consolidated information. We meta-learn how to consolidate using bi-level optimization at training time, where an inner loop encodes reasoning trajectories into a lightweight LoRA adapter, and an outer loop learns meta-parameters for the inner loop such that the consolidation is helpful for the model to synthesize a final solution. As no large-scale corpus of diverse reasoning trajectories exists for training aggregation methods, we construct the OpenParallelThinking corpus composed of 12,810 math problems paired with a mixture of trajectories from six LLMs. Evaluated on challenging math and STEM benchmarks, TTT-Consolidate outperforms the best aggregation baselines by up to 20 percentage points, even under matched compute and runtime settings, with the gap widening at larger model scales. TTT-Consolidate also recovers from unsuccessful individual trajectories more robustly, an ability that improves as the number of available (even incorrect) trajectories increases. Finally, we demonstrate that TTT-Consolidate benefits from both SFT and RL-based outer loop objectives. We will release TTT-Consolidate and OpenParallelThinking for use in future work on reasoning aggregation.

arxiv.titleZh: 用测试时训练整合推理
arxiv.summaryZh: 多路采样或多智能体的推理轨迹聚合时，投票只看结论会丢弃有用的中间推理，而把长轨迹直接拼进上下文又噪声过大。TTT-Consolidate 把多条推理轨迹当作适应数据:内层循环用测试时训练将轨迹编码进轻量 LoRA adapter，外层以双层优化元学习内层参数，使整合后的模型直接生成最终解。为此构建 OpenParallelThinking(12,810 道数学题配 6 个 LLM 的轨迹混合)，在数学与 STEM 基准上比最强聚合基线最高提升 20 个百分点，同算力同运行时下依然领先，且模型越大差距越明显;即使轨迹本身错误，数量增多也能提升恢复能力，SFT 与 RL 外层目标均有效。

arxiv.title: NorthCUA Technical Report: Turbocharging Computer-Use Agents through Experience at Scale
arxiv.abstract: Scaling computer-use agents from individual actions to complex software work requires experience that connects decisions to complete outcomes. We present NorthCUA, an integrated system for turbocharging computer-use agents through experience at scale. Its Experience Flywheel supplies diverse executable tasks to the NorthCUA Harness, which sustains long interactions, records decisions, and checks task outcomes. The Flywheel uses these records to curate verified trajectories. For unsolved tasks, recursive self-improvement evolves reusable skills and preserves verified milestones so later attempts build on earlier progress. Staged Learning combines this experience with grounding data from the Flywheel to develop GUI competence through mid-training and long-horizon supervised fine-tuning. The policy then learns from fresh attempts in the same Harness through joint desktop-web reinforcement learning, closing the loop between experience production and policy improvement. The resulting Nano, Mini, and Pro family achieves state-of-the-art results among open-source models across GUI grounding, desktop execution, and Web interaction under the reported evaluation settings. For more responsive Web workflows, NorthCUA-Ultrafast pairs direct action selection with open-ended generation on pre-RL Nano, offering a measured quality-latency tradeoff. Together, these advances establish NorthCUA as a high-performing model family and a reusable foundation for agents that carry complex software work from intent to completion.

arxiv.title: Bernoulli On-Policy Distillation: Don't Ignore High-Confidence Student Tokens
arxiv.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student language model on its own trajectories using token-level supervision from a stronger teacher. We show that standard sampled reverse-KL OPD systematically suppresses updates to high-confidence tokens, such that their weak gradient contribution does not necessarily imply weak or uninformative teacher supervision. We introduce Bernoulli On-Policy Distillation (Bernoulli OPD), which directly matches the teacher and student probabilities for that token. This yields a bounded probability space correction that preserves teacher-student disagreement while avoiding the additional confidence-dependent suppression induced by vanilla OPD. Fixed-rollout analyses show that Bernoulli OPD substantially restores optimization signal to high-confidence tokens while remaining sensitive to teacher-student disagreement. We further analyze the resulting model behavior through confidence distributions, answer calibration, policy movement, and training dynamics, showing that Bernoulli OPD's gains cannot be explained simply by longer reasoning, larger optimization steps, or more uniform imitation of the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/duterscmy/Bernoulli-OPD.
arxiv.comment: 14 pages, 7 figures, Code: https://github.com/duterscmy/Bernoulli-OPD
arxiv.titleZh: Bernoulli 同策略蒸馏：不要忽视学生模型的高置信度 token
arxiv.summaryZh: 标准采样的 reverse-KL 同策略蒸馏（OPD）会系统性压低学生高置信度 token 的更新权重，使这些 token 上的教师监督虽梯度弱却未必信息量低。Bernoulli OPD 对这类 token 直接匹配教师与学生的概率，给出有界的概率空间修正，既保留师生分歧，又避免原版 OPD 额外引入的、与置信度相关的抑制。固定 rollout 分析显示，该方法显著恢复了高置信度 token 的优化信号，并仍对师生分歧敏感；置信度分布、答案校准、策略位移与训练动力学分析进一步表明，其增益无法用更长推理、更大优化步长或更一致的教师模仿来解释，适用于对 token 级梯度分配敏感的蒸馏后训练实践。

arxiv.title: HQNN-CL: Regime-Aware Hybrid Quantum Neural Network with Continual Learning for Financial Forecasting
arxiv.abstract: Financial time-series forecasting is still difficult owing to the non-stationary nature of the market, regime changes, and catastrophic forgetting, which makes conventional deep learning models hard to adapt in the long term. To achieve uncertainty-aware robust financial forecasting in the face of changing market conditions, this study proposes a Hybrid Quantum-Classical Neural Network with Continual Learning (HQNN-CL). The proposed framework combines Gaussian Hidden Markov Model (HMM) based regime detection, BiLSTM temporal encoding, adaptive-depth parameterized quantum circuits, Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC), experience replay, and probabilistic forecasting in a single architecture. The framework was tested on four real-time stock datasets: Microsoft, Systems Limited, Teradata and Tata Consultancy Services, and compared with seven state-of-the-art forecasting models, including recurrent and Transformer-based models. The experimental results show that HQNN-CL has outperformed other methods on the Systems Limited (RMSE = 3.0149) and Teradata (RMSE = 0.8909) datasets and is within 0.32% and 0.40% of the best baseline method for Microsoft and Tata Consultancy Services, respectively. The proposed framework also generates well-calibrated probabilistic forecasts within the range of 89.5% to 96.5% empirical coverage rate, has zero catastrophic forgetting (BWT = 0.0000) for all sequential learning tasks, and consistently shows positive forward transfer. Ablation and statistical significance analyses also validate the performance of adaptive quantum feature learning and continual adaptation under heterogeneous market conditions, regime-wise.

arxiv.title: ParetoSaddler: Pareto-Guided Optimization of Agent Harnesses for Quality and Cost
arxiv.abstract: Harness optimization can substantially improve LLM agents without modifying model weights, but existing methods primarily optimize response quality. Extending them to joint quality--cost optimization introduces a challenge: applying the deployment preference during intermediate updates can prematurely reject candidates that are valuable for later improvements. We introduce ParetoSaddler, which addresses this mismatch by separating intermediate candidate promotion from final deployment selection. At each iteration, an optimizer updates a parent harness to produce a candidate, and then compares the two over repeated executions and uses Bayesian bootstrap Pareto support to promote candidates showing credible progress in either quality or cost. Promoted candidates receive broader development evaluation and remain available as parents for later optimization steps. We evaluate ParetoSaddler on ClawMark and GAIA2 using domain-disjoint splits. On ClawMark, ParetoSaddler improves quality from 70.86\% to 81.35\% while reducing cost from \$1.17 to \$1.01 per task; on GAIA2, it improves quality from 56.22\% to 62.89\% while reducing cost from \$0.78 to \$0.45 per task. The Pareto-selected harnesses also achieve higher quality at lower cost than quality-only harness optimization. Analysis shows that Pareto-aware optimization retains intermediate candidates that would be discarded by deployment preference but can support later improvements, while Bayesian bootstrap screening filters out candidates whose gains are weakly supported across runs.

arxiv.titleZh: ParetoSaddler：面向质量与成本的帕累托引导 Agent Harness 优化
arxiv.summaryZh: 现有 Agent harness 优化方法只关注回复质量，把目标扩展到质量与成本联合优化时会遇到一个错配：如果在中间更新阶段就套用部署偏好，就会过早淘汰对后续改进仍有价值的候选。ParetoSaddler 把中间候选晋升与最终部署选择分开：每轮由优化器将父 harness 改写为候选，重复执行后比较两者，并用 Bayesian bootstrap 估计的帕累托支持度晋升在质量或成本任一侧有可信进步的候选；被晋升的候选随后获得更大范围的开发评估，并继续作为后续优化的父代。在 ClawMark 上，质量由 70.86% 提升至 81.35%，每任务成本由 $1.17 降至 $1.01；在 GAIA2 上，质量由 56.22% 提升至 62.89%，成本由 $0.78 降至 $0.45，且帕累托选择得到的 harness 在质量与成本上都优于仅优化质量的做法。

arxiv.title: Decoupled Predictive Decision Making: A Shared Conditional Predictor for Agents
arxiv.abstract: Agent decisions depend on empirical relationships that deployment observations reveal and task descriptions alone may leave unresolved. We introduce Decoupled Predictive Decision Making (DPDM), an architecture that formulates heterogeneous agent decisions as conditional prediction with a shared pretrained learner. Language models provide semantic representations of current and historical records, while a general-purpose conditional predictor predicts task-defined targets from the represented evidence. Pretraining supplies reusable inference capability; deployment evidence instantiates problem-specific predictions without updating either model's neural parameters. Tool judgments, candidate preferences, and reasoning assessments share an evidence-and-query interface, with predictions mapped to choices by a decision rule. This architecture establishes complementary sources of agent capability: semantic knowledge acquired through language pretraining and empirical inference acquired through structured-data pretraining. A single frozen LimiX-2 predictor serves all five task categories. With Qwen3.5-27B as the semantic encoder, DPDM raises mean accuracy across 50 benchmarks from 78.80% with few-shot prompting to 84.92% under their respective evaluated history budgets, and reaches 82.33% with identical histories and queries. On ToolPRMBench's BFCL and ToolSandbox tasks, absolute accuracy gains are 34.26% and 28.87%, respectively, at the methods' respective evaluated history budgets. Accuracy improves as history grows. With identical imbalanced histories, mean balanced accuracy improves by an absolute 14.51% across five reasoning-step assessment tasks and four encoders. DPDM makes learning from experience an independently improvable foundation-model capability, creating a shared route for advances in conditional prediction to improve decisions across agent tasks.

arxiv.titleZh: 解耦的预测式决策:面向智能体的共享条件预测器
